scope: Actual ENSv2 mainnet bytecode on a disposable local Anvil fork, with the registrar source after the November 6 review fixes. Fixture operators are local test accounts, not public enrollments.

registrarAndPlanner: UserRegistry factory provenance and parent/subregistry attachment
Registrar register+renew root roles only; zero owner role bitmap accepted; transfer/resolver replacement refused
grantSetterRoles authorizes endpoint rotation only, not payee writes or another operator resolver
Authorized renewal, immediate registrar delisting naming the operator, curator-only reinstatement, revoked renewal refusal, and ENS expiry resolution removal
Lapsed operator cannot renew itself; an expired label is re-registered to a new owner through the registrar in the same slot, with the previous owner losing registrar rights
Unmodified staged planner gas estimates, exact root/name role counts, canonical receipt verification with 12 local confirmations
Deployment verifier rejects a genuine extra hot-key grant for an unknown text resource
Real fork registrar/resolver discovery using one injected local proof root per refresh; exact direct reference equality; altered proofs and identity mismatch rejected; renewal/removal/expiry applied
lifecycle: Exact reviewed sender/destination/calldata/value, manifest provenance, block preconditions, chain and unknown hot-key grants fail closed; signer/payee and cross-operator writes denied by actual ENS code

Allowed hot-key endpoint rotation has canonical before/receipt/current state evidence; twelve confirmations stay separate from an injected pending-finality tag; inconsistent receipt-block hashes rejected
Another managed-contract write in the same receipt block is rejected instead of being hidden by an end-of-block state match

Expired-but-active lease recovers through the registrar only by the curator, retaining owner/token/dedicated resolver; the operator cannot revive it; expiry bounds and unauthorized renewal reject; expired endpoint rotation refuses
Curator renewal and registrar delisting verified; delisting preserves token/owner/resolver/expiry, clears admission, and prevents renewal or implicit relisting
endpoints: Cold-owner migration is atomic: later inner-call failure rolls back revocation and records; paid and non-atomic/unreviewed migration evidence are rejected
Verified migration preserves original initialization history and limits the hot key to the entire plural record; singular/beacon/signer/payee and cross-operator writes deny
Post-audit reorg of the final observation rejects deployment verification
Plural lifecycle binds the full old/new list including beacon URLs; a concurrent edit to the other node, a forged old manifest observation and a head reorg during the finalized read are refused
Operator-wide delisting retains the plural record/token but clears admission; explicit reverse migration removes plural authority and restores only legacy authority
Fresh plural operator deployment completes every unsigned stage and canonical receipt/role verification with one dedicated resolver per operator

supersedes: The registrar behaviour described in ens-fork-evidence.json and ens-lifecycle-fork-evidence.json, which were recorded with the earlier registrar source: an operator could then renew its own lapsed lease, and removal took only an index.
reproduction: Start Anvil as a loopback mainnet fork, then run contracts/test/ens-fork.test.mjs with DERPC_ENS_FORK_RPC set. These checks do not establish a public deployment.
